body: The action at a distance here is a bit unsatisfying. I don't want to block the bugfix on it, but I'd like to know what browsers do here? That can also maybe resolve the comment thread you opened. Where do they keep this state? Maybe "script-blocking style sheet counter" is actually a set of `<link>` and `<style>` elements?? Changing to that wouldn't seem so bad.

> but I'd like to know what browsers do here? [...] Maybe "script-blocking style sheet counter" is actually a set of <link> and <style> elements?? Changing to that wouldn't seem so bad.

So it turns out that Chromium does indeed [maintain a set](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/loader/render_blocking_resource_manager.cc;l=144-161;drc=41482404045cb6689ea898d109dbdcfe3365a529) of all pending style sheets, a subset of which are [considered script-blocking](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/css/style_engine.cc;l=269-276;drc=41482404045cb6689ea898d109dbdcfe3365a529) and increment/decrement an associated counter.

The counter only gets incremented when an element is inserted into the set, and specifically when that element doesn't already appear in the set; this gives the counter set-like semantics where we can't double-count the same element. This is what I was getting at in the [thread above](https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/8552#discussion_r1032727308): each increment/decrement need to be associated with the (script-blocking status of the) _same_ request/response pair, so that if you rapidly initiate `N` different style sheet requests associated with the same `<link>` element, where `N-K` of them are script-blocking, in ["process this type of linked resource"](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#link-type-stylesheet:process-the-linked-resource) you decrement the counter `N-K` times, instead or just once depending on the script-blocking-ness of the last request. If we didn't do that, then the counter would remain artificially high forever.

But there's a larger problem going on here: all of this is trying to work around the weird behavior where if you rapidly make N different requests associated with the same element, each request will fully be made and invoke the "process this type of linked resource" response-handling steps, which I think is a bug separately from the issue this PR solves. In Chromium, each link stylesheet request that's made [ends up](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/core/html/link_style.cc;l=247-258;drc=8a27797c643fb0f2d9ae835f8d8b509e027c97e9):
 - Removing the element from the list of blocking style sheets
 - Decrementing the associated script-blocking counter
 - Quits observing load notification events from the fetching of the previous pending request

...thus resetting all of that pending state from the last unfinished request, if one existed. Depending on the script-blocking-ness of the _new_ request, that state _may_ be set again. But I don't think the spec does this, IIUC; it seems like for N rapidly-made requests (where each request is triggered before the last one finishes), we would end up firing N different load/error events, and maybe even processing N different style sheets, depending on response order??

The spec equivalent of the Chromium implementation (which I am assuming other browsers replicate) would be to have the [linked resource fetch setup steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#link-type-stylesheet:linked-resource-fetch-setup-steps) always remove the element from the script-blocking style sheet list if it's in there, and possibly re-adding it depending on the script-blocking-ness of the new request. What I have in this PR gets us closer to that, since we at least don't have a buggy counter anymore that can accidentally get double-incremented and never decremented depending on previous requests. But I still think we need some mechanism to stop observing old, unfinished requests so that we don't invoke the response-handling steps for each pending request made on the element. I think that, and the logic that removes elements from the script-blocking style sheet list upon new fetches, would make for a good follow-up that does all of the "Upon new request, unset old request state" work.
PR preview seems to have edited the OP saying there was a Wattsi build error even though all of the checks on this PR have passed?
